analysis.body: {"analysis":{"spec_version":"0.1.0","head":"d984d43dcfdbcc550479e7710856ddba73f5d6ca","analyses":[{"key":"","folder":".","label":"UNIONS weak lensing from ShapePipe's catalogue","description":"The UNIONS cosmic-shear analysis downstream of shape measurement. sample","description":"ShapePipe's run-1 snapshot (772,677,301 objects on 22,901 DR6 tiles) as a HATS shape catalogue; the v2 HATS collection that adds PhotoPipe's DR6 photometry and photo-z and PhotoPipe's spec-z matches to it, joined on the DR6 object ID; the comprehensive catalogue of every object with every ShapePipe and PhotoPipe column; and the calibrated cosmic-shear sample: the galaxy selection, the DES weight table, the metacalibration response of the weighted mean shear, the additive bias, and the calibrated shear R⁻¹(g − c_e) of each selected galaxy. Metacalibration measures each galaxy on five versions of its image, the branches: unsheared, and sheared by ±h (h = 0.01) along each shear component. The PSF and star catalogues come from the same snapshot. The tomographic bins, and the response of each bin, are made in the redshifts section.","tags":[],"declares":{"sp":""},"inputs":[],"decisions":[{"ref":"catalogue.decisions.overlap_cut","options":[{"id":"snapshot_tiles","label":"Neighbours among the snapshot's tiles","description":"The same cut however the catalogue is read.","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"tiles_in_hand","label":"Neighbours among the tiles being processed","description":"Keeps both copies wherever the neighbour is in another batch; correct only with the whole catalogue in memory at once.","tags":[],"insights":[]}],"label":"Tile-overlap cut on the snapshot's tile set","rationale":"Neighbouring tiles share a strip of sky, so an object there is detected and measured in both, and ShapePipe keeps both rows. Each object is kept only on its own tile's side of the RA midpoint to each neighbour and inside its tile's Dec range. A tile's neighbours are looked up among every tile of the snapshot, so the cut does not depend on how the catalogue is chunked, and a sample cannot be grown by appending tiles: 297 tiles lost 39,781 galaxies when run 1 grew from 20,515 to 22,901 tiles, each to a new neighbour.","tags":[]},{"ref":"catalogue.decisions.selection_cuts","options":[{"id":"bound_9_bit_16_ignored","label":"T/T_PSF < 9, FLAGS ignoring bit 16, no halo cut","description":"The v2.0.0 selection.","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"bound_3_strict_flags","label":"T/T_PSF < 3, FLAGS ≤ 2 on every bit","description":"The v1 selection; drops large galaxies and biases m in image simulations.","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"with_star_halos","label":"Also cut star halos (bits 1 and 2)","description":"Removes about 13% of the area; Paper III found the halo masking added B-modes in v1.","tags":[],"insights":[]}],"label":"Galaxy selection","rationale":"config/calibration/mask_v2.0.yaml: SExtractor FLAGS ≤ 2 ignoring bit 16 (incomplete aperture data, which preferentially flags large galaxies and biases m in image simulations); the overlap cut; outside star bodies, manual masks, MaxiMask and r-band gaps (mask bits 4, 8, 1024 and 64; the star-halo bits 1 and 2 are not cut); N_EPOCH ≥ 2; 15 ≤ mag ≤ 30; no ngmix moments failure, fitted at least once, and a valid PSF ellipticity; then on each metacal branch 10 < S/N < 500 and 0.707 < T/T_PSF < 9 with the branch's fit flag zero. The selection config is the input, so this decision is attached to the sample it makes. The release's catalogs/config_mask.yaml records these cuts as they ran.","tags":[]},{"ref":"catalogue.decisions.catalogue_match_tile_selection","options":[{"id":"no_cut","label":"No paired-fraction cut","description":"The paired fraction is a diagnostic.","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"cut_below_0_99","label":"Reject tiles below 0.99","description":"Removes 198 tiles and 675,307 selected galaxies (0.354% of the sample).","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"cut_below_0_995","label":"Reject tiles below 0.995","description":"Removes 3,072 tiles and 20,855,054 selected galaxies (10.92% of the sample).","tags":[],"insights":[]}],"label":"Tiles kept whatever their external paired fraction","rationale":"ShapePipe pairs each tile's detections with an external catalogue and records the paired fraction. No tile is removed on it. On the v2.0.0 selection all 18 measured tiles below 0.98 pairing yield no selected galaxy, because the N_EPOCH ≥ 2 cut empties them, so a 0.98 cut would remove nothing; stricter thresholds remove galaxies with no measured improvement. Reassess if the N_EPOCH cut is relaxed.","tags":[]},{"ref":"catalogue.decisions.sample_wide_calibration","options":[{"id":"one_for_the_sample","label":"One table and one response for the sample","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"refit_per_region","label":"Table and response per region of the footprint","description":"Follows depth variations, at the cost of noisier tables and a response that changes across the footprint.","tags":[],"insights":[]}],"label":"One weight table and one response for the whole sample","rationale":"The sample is weighted and calibrated as one population: one weight table fitted on every selected galaxy of the snapshot, and the whole sample's R and c_e applied to every row, not a table or response per region of the footprint. A weight depends on a galaxy only through its (S/N, size) cell, so the table and R follow from per-(tile, cell) sums that add over chunks of the catalogue. Each tomographic bin's own response is measured with this table held fixed, in the redshifts section.","tags":[]},{"ref":"catalogue.decisions.galaxy_weights","options":[{"id":"des_table_on_every_branch","label":"DES table at each branch's own S/N and size","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"frozen_weights","label":"Weights frozen at their unsheared values","description":"Removes the weight response from R.","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"inverse_variance","label":"Inverse-variance weights from each branch's errors","tags":[],"excluded":"The v2 shape catalogue does not keep the sheared branches' error columns.","insights":[]},{"id":"unit","label":"Unit weights","description":"Lower response and higher noise per galaxy.","tags":[],"insights":[]}],"label":"DES weight table evaluated on every branch","rationale":"Galaxies are weighted by a table W(S/N, size), with S/N = FLUX/FLUX_ERR and size = T/T_PSF of the ngmix fit, fitted on the unsheared branch and evaluated on every metacal branch at that branch's own S/N and size. A galaxy's weight therefore changes under shear, and the response includes that change. With unit weights the v2.0.0 sample has R = 0.6889, against 0.7869 with the table.","tags":[]},{"ref":"catalogue.decisions.weight_table","options":[{"id":"pooled_min_3","label":"20 × 20 cells, sparse cells pooled to 3 galaxies","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"no_pooling","label":"No pooling","description":"A sparse cell can carry an extreme weight.","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"pooled_min_10","label":"Sparse cells pooled to 10 galaxies","description":"Moves m in image simulations by up to 0.66σ for no gain in stability.","tags":[],"insights":[]}],"label":"The DES weight table","rationale":"In each (S/N, size) cell, W = (Σ r)² / (n Σ |e|²/2) over the n galaxies of the unsheared selection in it, with r the mean diagonal element of a galaxy's response and e its unsheared ellipticity; 20 × 20 logarithmic cells between the S/N and size cuts. A cell with fewer than 3 galaxies takes the moments of the smallest square of cells centred on it that holds 3. On the image-simulation grids, one cell of two galaxies without this pooling inflated one grid's error on m2 fivefold.","tags":[]},{"ref":"catalogue.decisions.response_estimator","options":[{"id":"separate_normalisation","label":"R_shear + R_selection, each branch on its own weight sum","tags":[],"insights":["catalogue.prior_insights.metacal_response","catalogue.prior_insights.metacal_selection"]},{"id":"joint","label":"Each sheared branch's own ellipticity under its own selection","description":"Agrees with the chosen R to 0.03% on v2.0.0; kept as a diagnostic.","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"common_denominator","label":"One weight sum for both sheared branches","description":"Drops the term from the change of the weight sum under shear.","tags":[],"insights":[]},{"id":"ivw_shear_unweighted_selection","label":"Inverse-variance R_shear with unweighted R_selection","description":"The earlier sp_validation practice; it calibrates a mean other than the weighted mean applied to the catalogue.","tags":[],"insights":[]}],"label":"Response of the weighted mean shear","rationale":"The catalogue's shear estimate is a weighted mean ⟨e⟩ = Σ w e / Σ w over a selection, and R calibrates it.
